results.title: 5 Technology Trends in Healthcare You Can’t Ignore in 2026 - KITRUM
results.content: At the same time, innovations in AI, remote monitoring, wearable devices, and virtual care are opening up new opportunities to improve outcomes, efficiency, and patient engagement. After years of pilot projects and scattered use, hospitals are now embedding AI tools directly into their workflow automation to relieve pressure on clinicians and improve patient care. Among other benefits of AI in healthcare are translation and communication tools, summarization and decision-support systems that provide relevant patient information, and automation of routine tasks, which frees up time for higher-value care. Plus, AI is transforming telehealth by analyzing patient data in real-time, supporting clinical decisions, and personalizing virtual care to improve outcomes and efficiency. While AI, wearables, and remote patient monitoring (RPM) provide powerful tools for clinicians, they also bring an increasing volume of data, which can contribute to cognitive overload. However, when thoughtfully integrated into workflows, RPM, wearables, and AI can reduce cognitive burden and support better patient care.

results.title: 10 future healthcare trends that will transform 2026 - Sermo
results.content: Value-based care is reshaping healthcare by rewarding providers for patient outcomes rather than the volume of services they deliver. These models emphasize improving patients’ health, reducing unnecessary costs, and leveraging technologies like data analytics and EHRs to track and report on outcomes and spending. Integrating mental health into primary care is now recognized as essential for improving patient outcomes. In a Sermo survey, we asked physicians, “How do you think wearable technology will change your approach to patient care in the next five years?” The leading responses show a mix of feelings about the clinical impact of wearable devices. 37% of physicians believe it will enable continuous monitoring and early intervention, thereby improving outcomes, while 29% anticipate it will create an overload of patient-generated data, making it more challenging to prioritize care. Integrating electronic health records and patient portals provides clinicians with real-time data, improving diagnostics and care coordination. For private practice owners and physicians, improving data interoperability means smoother patient care and less administrative hassle.

results.title: Digital Health Applications in Oncology: An Opportunity to Seize - PMC
results.content: Opportunities for digital health innovation in oncology include patient-facing technologies that improve patient experience, safety, and patient-clinician interactions; clinician-facing technologies that improve their ability to diagnose pathology and predict adverse events; and quality of care and research infrastructure to improve clinical workflows, documentation, decision support, and clinical trial monitoring. Based on proceedings of a 2020 workshop convened by the National Cancer Policy Forum of the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (4), we characterize the current state of digital health applications in oncology practice and research, highlight barriers to further implementation, and offer strategies to improve equitable use of digital health technologies to maximally improve outcomes for patients with cancer. Owing to the vast potential for digital health technologies to improve quality and reduce spending in cancer care, a 2020 National Cancer Policy Forum workshop convened leadership from oncology physician and nursing societies, cancer care practitioners, researchers, payers, policy makers, entrepreneurs, EHRs vendors, and patient and caregiver advocates to discuss opportunities for digital health in cancer care.
